data.content: Plan 2 days in Sigiriya for 2 Sri Lankan adults and 1 German adult, starting from Colombo; we want to climb the rock. We already have a hotel.

Wikivoyage guide for Sigiriya (all topics):
[Introduction] Sigiriya is a city in the Central District of Sri Lanka. The "Ancient City of Sigiriya" is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
[Understand] Sigiriya is famous for its high red stone fortress and palace ruins which are surrounded by the remains of an extensive network of gardens, reservoirs and other structures. The rock is believed by Hindus to be the site of the fortress of Ravana, the main villain in the epic Ramayana. There is also the Naipena Guhava (Cobra Hood Cave), which Hindus believe is where Ravana imprisoned Rama's wife Sita after kidnapping her. ...
[Get in] By bus: There are two transport hubs for getting to 1 Sigiriya bus stand. (updated May 2015) One is the bus station (locals call these bus stands) in Dambulla. The other is a much less built-up junction about half-way between Dambulla and Sigiriya, where the road to Sigiriya (B162) branches off the main highway (the A6), called Inamaluwa Junction. ...
[Get around] You can organise a tuk tuk to take you around, but most destinations are walkable if you're reasonably fit.
[See] Ancient City of Sigiriya: Entry fee to the site is US$15 for citizens of South Asian countries (passport required) and US$35 (Rs 11,500 as of Oct 2026) for those from other countries. These two groups have to buy their tickets inside the museum, not outside at the ticket office. Guides charge around Rs 2,000. ...
[Do] You don't necessarily have to spend big budget in Sigiriya to enjoy it. There are three rocks in the area which give you almost equally great views over the plains and especially onto the Lion Rock itself. 1 Duwannagala. The highest free rock, great for sunsets and sunrises. It also has a water facility building ontop which you can climb on and observe the surrounding plains and often spot elephants or other wildlife. ...
[Sleep] Budget: 1 Another World Hostel, ☏ +94778891592. A popular, clean and comfortable hostel. Has private rooms with private bathrooms, and 6 and 12 bed mixed dorms. Rs 4600 for standard dorm bed. (updated Oct 2026) Mid-range: 2 Aliya Resort and Spa, Avudangawa, ☏ +94 66 2040444, info@aliyaresort.com. The design is inspired by elephants hence the name "Aliya" which is the Sinhalese word for elephant. Rooms, chalets and suites are available. ...
[Stay safe] Bring lots of water as the walk through the gardens and the climb to the top of the rock takes about 1.5 hours. There is no water available inside the complex. It is possible to climb Sigiriya in the rain but care on the stone steps which become slippery when wet. Additionally, the view at the top might get obscured due to the rain. You'll see signs along the path telling you to be quiet so as not to provoke the wasps. ...

Wikivoyage guide for Sigiriya (see and do):
[See] Ancient City of Sigiriya: Entry fee to the site is US$15 for citizens of South Asian countries (passport required) and US$35 (Rs 11,500 as of Oct 2026) for those from other countries. These two groups have to buy their tickets inside the museum, not outside at the ticket office. Guides charge around Rs 2,000. They are helpful if you are travelling alone and want someone to take pictures of you, but otherwise they are only worthwhile if you want in-depth information about the history and culture of what you're looking at. There are noticeboards at each structure and landmark provide information. There is a path from the entrance to the complex to the rock. The gardens and other features are located on either sides of the pathway. 1 Sigiriya Lion Rock Fortress. 7:00-17:30. The plateau of Sigiriya rock is a lava dome elevated 200 m above the ground (and at a total elevation of 363 m above sea level). It can be reached through a combination of rock and metal stairs, some of which are only mounted at the side of the rock high above the ground. When facing the giant stone lion paws, you can see the construction and decide for yourself, whether you're up for the experience. ...
[Do] You don't necessarily have to spend big budget in Sigiriya to enjoy it. There are three rocks in the area which give you almost equally great views over the plains and especially onto the Lion Rock itself. 1 Duwannagala. The highest free rock, great for sunsets and sunrises. It also has a water facility building ontop which you can climb on and observe the surrounding plains and often spot elephants or other wildlife. (updated Jan 2025) 2 Mapagala. Just south of Sigiriya, even though Pidurangala is hidden from this view. (updated Jan 2025) 3 Melu’s Rock. It seems like it is only accessible by walking through one of the two resorts that are nearby, but non-guests are allowed through. It has great views of Sigiriya and Pidurangala and a large Buddha statue nearby. (updated Jan 2025)

# 2-day trip to Sigiriya

A 2-day itinerary from Colombo to Sigiriya tailored for 2 Sri Lankan adults and 1 German adult. Highlights include climbing the iconic Sigiriya Lion Rock Fortress, exploring historical caves, and visiting panoramic surrounding rocks like Duwannagala, Mapagala, and Melu's Rock.

**Starting point:** Colombo

## Day 1: Travel from Colombo & Sunset Viewpoints
*Weather:* 2026-11-23: moderate rain showers; min 23.2 °C, max 29.9 °C; chance of precipitation 98%; rainfall 7.0 mm; max wind 11.4 km/h (Open-Meteo)
*Travel:* Colombo to Sigiriya: 165 km, about 3 h 6 min by car without traffic (OSRM)
- **Afternoon: Duwannagala** (about 2 h) - Climb this nearby free rock for panoramic views over the surrounding plains and to observe local wildlife. _(Wikivoyage)_
- **Evening: Mapagala** (about 1.5 h) - Explore Mapagala, situated just south of Sigiriya, for evening views over the surrounding landscape. _(Wikivoyage)_

## Day 2: Sigiriya Rock Climb & Historic Sights
*Weather:* 2026-11-24: thunderstorm; min 23.0 °C, max 28.2 °C; chance of precipitation 100%; rainfall 9.9 mm; max wind 15.8 km/h (Open-Meteo)
- **Morning: Sigiriya Lion Rock Fortress** (about 3.5 h) - Climb the UNESCO World Heritage site via the rock and metal staircases to explore the ancient fortress and palace ruins. _(Wikivoyage)_
- **Afternoon: Naipena Guhava** (about 1 h) - Visit the Cobra Hood Cave, a natural rock overhang featuring ancient inscriptions and cave structures. _(Wikivoyage)_
- **Evening: Melu’s Rock** (about 1.5 h) - Enjoy views of Sigiriya Rock and Pidurangala from Melu's Rock and visit the large Buddha statue nearby. _(Wikivoyage)_

## Entrance fees (official sources)

- Driving from Colombo to Sigiriya covers 165 km and takes approximately 3 hours and 6 minutes by car in free-flowing traffic. _(OSRM)_
- The climb to the top of Sigiriya Lion Rock Fortress takes around 1.5 hours and there is no drinking water available inside the site complex. _(Wikivoyage)_
- Visitors are instructed to remain quiet along the climbing trail to avoid provoking nesting wasps. _(Wikivoyage)_
